channel.project_pack_ref: Standardised Corporate Tax Filing Workflow Rollout

threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, key deliverables and roles for the tax workflow project.

messages.text: Hi team, kicking off the new 'Standardised Corporate Tax Filing Workflow' project. The main goal is to reduce errors and standardise our process. I've reviewed the initial brief, and the key deliverables seem to be the process map, checklists, a central calendar, and various guidelines. Let's confirm the scope and who is owning what. All thoughts are welcome.

Thanks for starting this. From my side, I can take on the administrative tasks like creating the centralised calendar and setting up the shared folder structure. I can also help compile the final training pack once the core documents are ready.
Sounds good. For the scope, are we including all client segments from the start, or just the monthly filers? Starting with a smaller group might be easier.

I can start mapping the current process for T1 right away. I've already got some notes on this. I can also draft the quality review procedure for T5. We should be able to get all drafts done this week.

Good point. The project brief mentions piloting with a subset of clients. I suggest we focus on the 'SME monthly' and 'Corporate quarterly' filers first. They cover most of our volume and have the most recurring issues.
I agree with that approach. Let's formalise that. For the first rollout, we will focus on the SME monthly and Corporate quarterly filing cycles. That seems manageable and will give us good data.
Ok, so T1 will focus only on those segments. That simplifies it. But the RACI in A1 needs to be clear for everyone, not just those segments.

Correct. The process map for T1 will be for the pilot segments, but the RACI defined in A1 and the sign-off procedure from T5 should be designed to be scalable for all clients eventually. Let's make sure the documents reflect that.
So who is taking the lead on the other deliverables, like the main checklist and the retention guidelines?
I can take the first pass at the preparation checklist and the error analysis. My audit background should help there.
I can work on the documentation and retention guidelines. That leaves the query handling procedure and the filing status tracker.
I can draft the status tracker. A simple spreadsheet should work, right?
I'll take the query handling procedure then. I'll add it to my list with T1 and T5.

Okay, that's a lot for one person. Let's distribute this a bit more. How about this: @48446 you focus on T1 (process map) and T5 (sign-off). @104021 on T2 (checklist) and T8 (error analysis). @390807 on T11 (status tracker). I'll take T4 (retention) and T9 (query handling). @497040 has the admin tasks T3, T6, T7. Does that work?
Works for me.
Yes, that's clear.
Confirmed.
Fine by me. T1 and T5 it is.
Great. So we have our owners. Let's lock that in as our initial plan. We can adjust as we go. This confirms the final list of project deliverables and roles.

threads.thread_goal: Design and iterate on the tax return preparation checklist and review steps.

messages.text: Team, here is the first draft of the 'Tax Return Preparation and Review Checklist' (A2) for T2. I've structured it into sections: Data Collection, Calculation, Initial Review, and Final Sign-off. Please take a look and let me know your thoughts.
Thanks! This looks like a good start. It's very detailed. Will there be a separate version for different client types or is this one-size-fits-all?

I've reviewed it. It covers the core calculation steps well. However, I don't see any specific checks for potential fraud red flags. We should add a section for that, maybe cross-referencing common issues from T8.
The idea is to have a master checklist (A2) that covers 90% of cases. We can add optional sections for specific industries if needed, but let's start with a common base.

Good point. I was thinking about that. Should we have a separate 'Fraud Detection' section, or embed those checks within the existing sections? For example, a check for unusual expense claims could go under the 'Calculation' part.

Embedding them makes more sense from a workflow perspective. It ensures they are checked at the right stage. We can use the output of T8, the 'Top Recurring Errors' analysis, to build these checks. Let's create a specific list of 3-5 mandatory red-flag checks and integrate them directly into the relevant steps of A2.

I agree. That makes the checklist more actionable. Also, could we add a hyperlink in the checklist document to the 'Top Recurring Tax Filing Errors' doc (A7) for reference? It would be helpful for training new staff.
Great idea, I'll add the link. I'm also working on T8 concurrently, so I'll have the initial list of errors by tomorrow. I can then integrate the red-flag checks into the next version of A2.
So the structure will be: Data Collection, Calculation (with embedded red-flag checks), Initial Review, Final Sign-off. That works for me. It's logical.

Yes, but the 'Initial Review' section needs to be very clear about what is being checked. Is it just arithmetic, or also a check against prior year filings? We need to define the scope of that review.

Good point. Let's specify that the 'Initial Review' includes: 1) Arithmetical accuracy, 2) Consistency with source documents, and 3) A high-level variance analysis against the previous period. @104021 can you add those sub-points?
Will do. Thanks for the feedback everyone. I'll incorporate these changes.
Perfect. With those additions, I think we can approve the overall structure and the mandatory items for the checklist. Let's move forward with this plan.

threads.thread_goal: Set up and validate the deadlines calendar and filing status control sheet.

messages.text: Hi all, as per T3 and T11, I've created the first versions of the 'Tax Deadlines and Obligations Calendar' (A3) and the 'Tax Filing Status Control Sheet' (A6). You can find them in the shared project folder. Please review and let me know if any deadlines are missing or if the control sheet needs more fields.
Thanks @497040! I've checked the control sheet A6. It has client name, filing type, due date, preparer, and status. This is great. Should we add a column for the reviewer as well?
The calendar A3 looks comprehensive for the SME and Corporate clients. I cross-checked a few of our more complex quarterly filers and their deadlines are all there. Good work.
Good suggestion. Adding a 'Reviewer' column makes sense to track handoffs. I'll add it right now.

Yes, a 'Reviewer' column is essential. I'd also suggest a 'Date Submitted' column to close the loop. So the minimum fields would be: Client, Filing Type, Due Date, Preparer, Reviewer, Status, Date Submitted.
Done. I've added 'Reviewer' and 'Date Submitted' to A6. The sheet is updated.
What about non-standard filings, like extensions or amended returns? Should we track those in A6 or somewhere else?

For now, let's keep A6 focused on the standard, recurring filings to keep it clean. We can add non-standard ones as separate line items if they come up, using the 'Filing Type' column to specify 'Amended' or 'Extension'. Let's not overcomplicate it at the start.
Okay, that works.
Great. So we agree on those minimum required fields for the filing status control sheet A6. I think that's settled.
For the calendar A3, are we only tracking the final submission deadlines, or also internal deadlines for preparation and review?
Right now it's just the official submission deadlines. I've set automated reminders for 14 days and 7 days before each deadline. We can add internal milestones if the team finds it useful.

Let's stick to the official deadlines in the shared calendar A3 to avoid clutter. We can manage our internal timelines using the control sheet A6. So, we confirm that the calendar will track the official submission deadlines for all SME monthly and Corporate quarterly clients.
Sounds like a good plan. The separation of concerns is clear.

threads.thread_goal: Close on documentation, retention and query handling guidelines.

messages.text: Team, I've drafted the 'Tax Documentation and Retention Policy' (A4) for T4 and the 'Handling Tax Authority Queries' procedure (A8) for T9. They are in the project folder. Please review and provide feedback, especially on the retention periods and the escalation steps.
I've also finished the draft for the 'Quality Review and Sign-off Procedure' (A5). It's in the folder now. It complements the retention policy.

Thanks. On A8, the query handling doc, the steps for logging and initial response are clear. From my audit experience, it's critical to have a strict timeline for escalating unanswered queries. I suggest we add a hard rule: 'escalate to compliance manager if no response plan is in place within 48 hours'.
That's a great point, very practical. I'll add that 48-hour escalation rule to A8. With that change, are we comfortable approving the procedure for handling tax authority queries?

Looking at A4, the retention policy. The periods listed (e.g., 7 years for core returns) seem standard. The storage rules mention a 'central archive folder'. Is this the same shared folder structure @497040 is setting up for T6?
Yes, exactly. The guidelines in A4 will define the rules, and the folder structure from T6 will be the practical implementation. I'll make sure the naming conventions match.
We also need a process for updating these documents when tax rules change, as per T12. Should we add a section in A4 about an annual review?

Yes, I've started a separate document for the update process (T12). It will state that all guidelines (A4, A5, A8) must be reviewed annually or whenever major tax legislation is passed. Let's keep that process separate from the guidelines themselves to avoid confusion.
Ok, but the A4 document itself should at least mention that it is subject to periodic review. A simple footer would be enough.

Fair enough. I'll add a 'Review Date' and 'Next Review' field to the footer of all guideline docs. With that, are we happy to approve the documentation retention periods and storage rules as laid out in A4?
Yes, looks good.
Agreed.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and debrief the pilot run of the new workflow on selected clients.

messages.text: Hello team, it's time to plan the pilot run for our new workflow (T10). I've drafted a proposal with a list of 5 clients (3 SME monthly, 2 Corporate quarterly) and a timeline that aligns with their upcoming filing dates. The document is in the project folder. Please review and let's finalize the plan.

Thanks! I see 'Client Corp B' is on the list. They have some complex international transactions. Are we sure they're a good candidate for the very first pilot? Maybe we should start with a more straightforward quarterly filer.

I think we should keep them. If the process works for a complex client, it will work for anyone. We need to stress-test the system. In fact, I think 5 clients is too few, we should do at least 10 to get proper data.

Let's find a middle ground. The goal of the pilot is to identify major flaws, not to achieve statistical significance. @390807 has a valid point about starting simple. How about we swap 'Client Corp B' for 'Client Corp C', which is more typical? And let's stick with 5 clients to ensure we can provide proper support and gather detailed feedback without overwhelming ourselves.

I agree with that adjustment. A controlled pilot is better. The proposed timeline looks tight but feasible if we're all focused. We'll be using the new checklist A2 and control sheet A6 for this, correct?

Correct. We'll use all the new artifacts: the process map A1, checklist A2, calendar A3, and control sheet A6. I've updated the pilot client list to swap Corp B for Corp C. If everyone agrees, we can lock in this list and timeline.
Works for me. Now, how do we collect feedback during the pilot?
I was thinking we could hold a 30-minute debrief meeting after each pilot filing is submitted. We can also have a shared document where people can log issues or suggestions in real-time.
Meetings are slow. A shared doc is better. We should just put all feedback there and review it at the end of the pilot cycle.

A combination of both is probably best. The shared doc is great for capturing immediate thoughts, but a short debrief call allows for discussion and clarification. Let's agree to use a shared feedback log AND schedule a brief 30-min sync after the last pilot filing is complete to discuss the key themes.
That's a solid plan. It balances async input with synchronous discussion.

Excellent. I'll set up the shared feedback doc and schedule the debrief meeting. I also need to finalize the training pack (T7) and the shared folder structure (T6) before we kick off. I'll have that done by EOD tomorrow.
